packageRules.description: Runtime dependencies are ranges, not pins, because users resolve them fresh on every install; our lockfile isn't published. A pin holds users on whatever version our last release happened to have, so a fix (security or otherwise) reaches them only once we publish again, and npm installs a second copy whenever the user's project already has a newer one. :pinOnlyDevDependencies would use 'replace', which ignores in-range releases entirely. 'update-lockfile' still opens a PR for each one, so CI tests the same versions users are getting, and those lockfile-only PRs are safe to automerge because they change nothing in the published package. A release outside the range rewrites the range in package.json; that change ships to users, so it needs a release. A repo whose dependencies are part of its contract, such as a lint config, can pin them again locally.

This repo publishes to npm, so its peerDependencies are a constraint on consumers rather than a choice for this repo. Pinning them would force every downstream consumer onto one exact version. :pinOnlyDevDependencies would 'widen' them instead (^10 becomes ^10 || ^11), which claims the old major still works when CI only tests the newest one from the lockfile. Replace the range only when it no longer matches. A repo that tests each supported peer major in CI can opt into 'widen' locally.
